The appellant before this Court was a claimant in a case under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988, and is aggrieved by the Judgment and Award dated 31-08-2019 passed by Learned Additional District Judge Malbazar Jalpaiguri in MAC case No-323 of 2017.

The case of the appellant before the Learned Trial Court may be summed up thus:
On 24-07-2016 at about 1.00 Hrs. when the said Soumendra Nath Saha was returning to the Parental house of the appellant from Siliguri towards Prakash Nagar on his motor cycle bearing Registration number WB-74-AJ- 1741 at that time near Payal More, P.S. Bhaktinagar District Jalpaiguri a pick up van bearing Regd. No.

sentences.text: Soumendra Nath Saha received severe injuries on his person and was shifted to Anandaloke Hospital where the attending doctor declared him dead.

Being unable to obtain any compensation in respect of the death of Soumendra Nath Saha the petitioners being the wife has been compelled to file this case praying for compensation of Rs. 42,00,000/- along with interest.
The Respondent no-2 Oriental Insurance Company filed written statement and contested the case.
ISSUES were framed and evidence was adduced by the claimant/appellant.

Upon perusing the evidence adduced and upon hearing the parties Learned Trial Court was pleased to dispose of the claim case by observing and directing as follows 'Hence it is ORDERED that the application U/S. 166 of the MV Act be and the same is allowed ex-parte against the owner of the offending vehicle and on contest against the O.P. no. 2/Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. without cost.

The claimant do get an award of Rs. 21,64,468/- (Rupees Twenty One Lakhs Sixty four thousand four hundred and sixty eight only) along with simple interest @ 9% p.a. from the date of institution of this case ie. 25.08.2017.

Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd. is directed to pay a sum of Rs. 21,64,468/- (Rupees Twenty One lakh Sixty Four thousand four hundred and sixty eight only) along with simple interest @ 9% p.a. from the date of institution of this case ie. 25-08-2017 by issuing one Account payee cheque in the name of Priyanka Saha (Nandi) within one month from the date of this Judgment in default

it shall carry simple interest @ 9%
p.a. from date till its full realization.'
The claimant/Appellant being aggrieved by the Judgment and Award dated 31-08-2019 has come up with the instant appeal.
The ground on which the Judgment is assailed is that the Learned Trial Judge failed to assess the proper annual income of the victim/deceased and fixing fictitious reasonable annual income.
Secondly the Learned Trial Judge failed to appreciate that as per last Income Tax Return of the deceased his gross annual income was Rs.
( Rupees three Lakh Forty One Thousand Five Hundred Sixty)
. It is also submitted that the correct multiplier is also not applied.
Heard learned Advocate for the appellant, and learned Advocate for the respondent no-1.
Perused the materials on record.
Learned Advocate for the appellant/claimant submits that the Learned Trial Judge erred in not considering the income tax return document filed by the claimant which was marked exhibit with objection.

Learned Advocate for he respondent no. 1 Insurance Company submits that the income tax return filed by the claimant/appellant was Xerox copy thus the Learned Trial Judge rightly refused to rely on the said documents.

In the case of Shipra Brahma and others (supra) a Learned Co-ordinate Bench of this Hon'ble Court was pleased to observe as follows:
'21.
Learned Lawyer for the claimants argues that as the Income Tax Return is a public document, the learned Tribunal ought to have admitted the", Income Tax Return in evidence.
In support of his contention learned lawyer has cited a decision dated 14.02.2020 rendered by a Single Bench of, Telangana High Court in Civil Revision Petition Nos. 3087 & 3133 of 2019.
At paragraph 9 of the decision the learned Single Bench of the, Hon'ble Telangana High Court has held that Income Tax Returns are public documents and they can be summoned by the Court.

Mr. Rajesh,
Singh, learned lawyer for the Insurance Company by citing a decision dated 01.08.2007 rendered by a Division Bench of this High Court in FMA No.", 108 of 2006 (Minara Begum and Ors.-Vs- National Insurance Company Limited and Ors.)
submits that this Hon'ble Court has held that if Income, Tax Officer is not called upon to prove the authenticity of Income Tax return, copy of the Income Tax return filed by the party cannot be relied upon.",
22.
Perusal of the case records shows that the claimants filed Income Tax Returns in original for the financial years 2007-08 and 2008-09.
But, they", filed a photocopy of the Income Tax Return for the assessment year 2009-10.

In such factual aspect and in view of the decision of the Division Bench, of this Court in FMA No.
108 of 2006 (Minara Begum and Ors.-Vs- National Insurance Company Limited and Ors.) , I hold that the learned Tribunal", rightly refused to admit the photocopy of the Income Tax Return for the year 2009-10 in evidence sans its proper proof.'

sentences.text: Before proceeding to decide the material in issue regarding quantum of compensation it is to be remembered that Income Tax Return is the most authentic document regarding income of a person as held in different judicial pronouncements.

As the plea raised by the Learned Counsel for the respondent no-1. United India Insurance Company Limited that the Income Tax Return submitted was a Xerox copy and as per the decision of Shipra Brahma and others (supra) a co-ordinate Bench of this Court upheld the decision of the tribunal in not accepting the photocopy of Income Tax Return this Court is of the view that the facts of this case are different
In Shipra Brahma the Learned Tribunal refused to admit the photocopy of the Income Tax Return but in the instant case the Income Tax Return was marked exhibit with objection.
The purpose of marking Income Tax Return as Exhibit with objection is to grant Insurance Companies opportunity to make necessary Enquires from the Income Tax Authority about its genuineness.

In the event the Insurance Companies are satisfied about its genuineness the said Companies should not stand in the way of the document being taken into consideration for determining compensation as the object of Insurance Companies is to see that genuine claims are honoured.

On the other hand Priyanka Saha vs Narayan Rakshit & Anr on 22 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175016600/

sentences.text: if the Insurance Companies find after enquiry that the Income Tax Return document is not genuine report should be submitted before the tribunal.

As Insurance Companies conduct enquiry when claim is made before them in some cases prior to approaching tribunal and sometimes claims are settled at a pre-litigation stage when it is found genuine by Insurance Companies, similarly in case of claim before tribunal the Insurance Company is to see that genuine claims are honoured.

As claim before tribunal is not a regular suit but a Quasi Judicial Proceedings Courts may instead of insisting claimants to prove Income Tax Return by examining Income Tax Authorities may exhibit the Income Tax Return with objection and permit the Insurance Companies to make necessary enquiries with regard to the said document and submit report before Court accordingly.
In the instant case pursuant to the Income Tax Return being marked exhibit with objection no enquiry was made and no report by respondent no-1 Insurance Company was submitted.

Only on the submission of the Learned Advocate for the respondent no-01 United India Insurance Company Ltd that the Income Tax Return cannot be taken to be sacrosanct the Learned Court refused to consider Income Tax Return.
Thus the Income Tax Return should be taken into consideration for the purpose of computing compensation.

As per the Income Tax Return Total yearly income is Rs. 2,14,780/- 40% should be added as future prospect As 40% is Rs. 85,912/- the annual income after adding future prospect comes to Rs.
300,692/- 1/3rd should be deducted on account of personal expenses.

As 1/3rd comes to Rs.
100,230/- this amount deducted from Rs. 300,692/- the annual dependency loss comes to Rs.
200,462/-.
The Multiplier of 17 should be applied.

Thus the total dependency loss comes to Rs.
34,07,854/-.
Further the Appellant claimant is entitled to Rs. 70,000/- on account of loss of consortium loss of estate and funeral expenses.
Thus the total compensation which comes by arithmetical calculation is Rs. 34,77,854/-.

However this court is of the view that Rs. 34,00,000/- is just and reasonable compensation, which the claimant/appellant is entitled to from the respondent no-1 United India Insurance Company L:imited.
As Learned Trial Court has already awarded interest @ 9% per annum no further interest is awarded on the excess sum.
Hence this appeal stands disposed.

Judgment and Award dated 31-08- 2019 passed by Learned Additional District Judge Malbazar Jalpaiguri in MACC Case No-323 of 2017 stands modified to the extent that the Appellant/claimant is entitled to compensation of Rs. 34,00,000/- from respondent no-1 United India Insurance Company Limited.
However there will be no order as to interest on the excess amount as observed above.
The respondent no-1 shall deposit Rs. 34,00,000/- less the Principal amount already paid in terms of the Judgment and Award of the Learned Trial Court.
In the event the Order of the Trial Court is not complied the amount as directed by the trial Court along with interest plus Rs. 12,35,532/- shall be deposited.
Such deposit shall be made before Registrar Circuit Bench High Court Calcutta within 5 weeks from the date of communication of this Order.
